name: Esther Vergeer
one_line: Won her last 470 matches in a row across ten years and retired at 31 without being beaten again.

facts.claim: won 470 consecutive singles matches; the streak ran from early 2003 until her retirement in February 2013 - ten straight years unbeaten
facts.note: The streak ended by RETIREMENT, not defeat. Nobody ever beat her again.

facts.claim: her last defeat was on 30 January 2003, to Daniela di Toro at the Sydney International
facts.note: Useful framing: name the LAST HUMAN to beat her, then the date, then silence.

facts.claim: lost only 18 sets in the 470-match streak
at least 452 of the 470 streak wins were in straight sets - she lost only 18 sets total, and each dropped set can account for at most one three-set match
facts.note: DERIVED: 470 matches minus at most 18 that could have reached a deciding set. Phrase as 'never even reached a deciding set'.

facts.claim: faced exactly one match point in the entire ten-year streak - Korie Homan, in the 2008 Beijing Paralympic final - and saved it
facts.note: THE story beat. One point from losing, once in a decade, in a Paralympic final - then unbeaten for four more years after it. Commons has a photo of her SERVING at Beijing 2008 (File:080908 - Esther Vergeer serves).

facts.claim: world No. 1 for 668 weeks, relinquished 21 January 2013 only because she retired
seven Paralympic gold medals (four singles: Sydney 2000, Athens 2004, Beijing 2008, London 2012; three doubles), plus one silver
paralyzed at age 8: a swimming accident at 6 revealed a vascular condition around her spinal cord; a nine-hour operation on 15 January 1990 left her unable to move her legs
facts.note: Born 18 July 1981, so the operation came at age 8. She learned tennis in rehabilitation.

facts.claim: retired in February 2013, aged 31, with the streak intact
first reached world No. 1 on 6 April 1999, aged 17
facts.note: DERIVED age: born 18 July 1981, ranking date 6 April 1999 = 17. Bridges the origin to the 2003 loss - she was already No. 1 when di Toro beat her.

facts.claim: won 120 successive tournaments in her final decade
facts.note: IPC verbatim: 'she won 120 successive tournaments in the final decade.' Note: IPC counts 44 Grand Slam titles vs Wikipedia's 43 - stick with 43 (Wikipedia's itemized count) or say 'more than forty'.

facts.claim: called, by the International Paralympic Committee, arguably the greatest individual ever to have played the game
facts.note: Backs the question-hook 'is she the most dominant athlete of all time?' - the video poses the question, the IPC quote and the numbers answer it.

facts.claim: the longest winning streak in able-bodied professional tennis is Martina Navratilova's 74 straight matches (1984)
facts.note: Wikipedia: 'a record for a professional'. The gap framing: the best tennis streak ever recorded on two feet is 74; hers is 470. Do NOT claim hers is the longest streak in all of sport (Jahangir Khan's squash run is longer).

comparison.gap_description: 470 straight wins over ten years; the best anyone has done on two feet is 74.

story_beat: In ten years and 470 matches, she faced exactly one match point - in the 2008 Beijing Paralympic final, against Korie Homan. She saved it, won the final, and was never beaten again for the rest of her career.
